title: The Leeward Escarpment
premise: Petra Brightwater, a salvage diver drowning in debt, is salvaging a wreck the navy quietly forbids anyone to discuss when a dying prospector trades her a map for one promise: finish what he started. The map points to the Leeward Escarpment, where a sunken colonial treasure ship holds not gold but proof of who truly inherited the region's shipping fortune — evidence that could ruin the fleet magnate whose salvage armada is already hunting the same wreck. Racing six tides against the fleet, Petra discovers the prospector was her grandfather, that her compass is the inheritance key, and that the magnate is her own estranged father. In the flooded hold, she must choose between selling the proof for her freedom or burning it and claiming an identity no one can buy; she burns it, sinks the fleet's claim, and surfaces owning nothing but herself.
about_author: Orsen Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade mapping wrecks off windward coasts before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who trade everything for one honest thing.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Petra Brightwater dives a forbidden wreck under contract, finding a sealed strongbox stamped with a crest she doesn't recognize. Her handler confiscates it and warns her off. POV Petra. Beat: restless competence shadowed by debt and unease.

chapters.title: A Debt in Salt Water
chapters.summary: Petra's creditors give her six days before they take her boat, the Kestrel. She takes a desperate night job towing a stranger out past the reef line. POV Petra. Beat: cornered pragmatism, the first crack of fate opening.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: The stranger, old Silas Vane, is shot by men following him. Dying aboard the Kestrel, he trades Petra a wax-sealed map for a promise: carry it to the Escarpment, tell no one. POV Petra. Beat: grief and dread braided together.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Deciphering Vane's map, Petra finds the Leeward Escarpment marked with her own family name — Brightwater — beside a crest matching the confiscated strongbox. POV Petra. Beat: vertigo of identity, the personal intruding on the professional.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Harbor gossip reveals the Corvane Salvage Fleet is provisioning for the same coordinates, led by magnate Aldous Corvane himself. Petra calculates she has six tides' head start. POV Petra. Beat: cold resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Crew of Two
chapters.summary: Petra reluctantly signs on Juno Reyes, a disgraced naval cartographer who recognizes the crest and wants revenge on Corvane. They argue over trust, then cast off at dawn. POV alternating Petra/Juno. Beat: wary alliance forged from mutual damage.

chapters.title: Tailwind and Traitors
chapters.summary: A Corvane tender shadows them through the straits; Juno rigs a false heading while Petra runs dark without lights through a minefield of reefs. POV Juno. Beat: first test passed, trust tentatively earned.

chapters.title: The Navy Won't Discuss It
chapters.summary: A navy patrol boards them, confiscates their charts, and lets them go with a warning — confirming someone powerful wants the Escarpment buried. Petra realizes the wreck predates any salvage claim. POV Petra. Beat: paranoia sharpening into understanding.

chapters.title: Storm Glass
chapters.summary: A squall forces them into a hidden cove where they find Vane's abandoned camp: journals proving he spent thirty years searching, and a photograph of a woman wearing Petra's compass. POV Petra. Beat: the past reaching forward, tenderness amid danger.

chapters.title: Blood and Brass
chapters.summary: Juno deciphers the journals: the Brightwater fortune was stolen from Vane's sister, Petra's grandmother, by the man who became Corvane's partner. The compass is a cipher key. POV Juno. Beat: fury and revelation, stakes turning intimate.

chapters.title: The First Tide Turns
chapters.summary: They reach the Escarpment as the Corvane fleet appears on the horizon, two tides ahead of schedule. Petra dives the drop-off alone and finds the wreck's mast, wrapped in navy cable. POV Petra. Beat: awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Down the Throat
chapters.summary: Petra penetrates the flooded hold through a collapsed gunport, nearly dies in a silt-out, and locates the sealed archive room — locked, needing the compass. POV Petra. Beat: terror mastered by discipline; the prize within reach.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Aboard the fleet flagship, Aldous Corvane offers Petra a fortune to walk away — then reveals he knows her name, her father's name, and calls her his daughter. POV Petra. Beat: the ground of identity giving way entirely.

chapters.title: Father of the Fleet
chapters.summary: Petra confronts Corvane privately; he claims Vane stole from him, spins the theft backward. She neither accepts nor refuses, buying time while Juno copies the fleet's dive schedule. POV Petra. Beat: dangerous performance, rage held behind glass.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Corvane's divers cut the Kestrel loose and scuttle her dinghy; Juno is caught copying charts and thrown in the brig. Petra escapes the flagship by diving off at night. POV Juno. Beat: betrayal's cost, isolation at its lowest point.

chapters.title: Alone on the Escarpment
chapters.summary: Stranded with a rebreather and the compass, Petra makes three dives in deteriorating weather, finally cracking the archive lock using the compass's cipher ring. POV Petra. Beat: solitary endurance, the self stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Hold of Proof
chapters.summary: Inside: the original partnership deed, grandmother's letters, and Corvane's confession of murder — enough to destroy him and restore the Brightwater name. Petra also finds Vane's final letter to her. POV Petra. Beat: grief, vindication, and the weight of choice.

chapters.title: Two Tides Left
chapters.summary: Surface storm traps Petra on a skerry; she reads Vane's letter, learning he chose her not for blood but because she finishes what she promises. She resolves to free Juno first. POV Petra. Beat: identity chosen rather than inherited.

chapters.title: Burning the Deed
chapters.summary: Petra infiltrates the flagship, frees Juno, and — before Corvane's eyes — feeds the deed and letters into the engine furnace: proof destroyed means his empire stands, but on lies he can never escape. POV Petra. Beat: climax; power renounced to defeat corruption.

chapters.title: The Fall of Corvane
chapters.summary: Juno broadcasts what she memorized of the confession to every crew and port authority in range; the fleet's captains mutiny, the navy arrives to arrest Corvane, who screams after Petra that she is still his blood. POV Juno. Beat: cathartic collapse of the corrupt.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Wreckage settled, debts voided by Corvane's arrest, Petra and Juno raise the Kestrel and dive the Escarpment one last time — not for treasure, but to lay Vane's compass on the wreck as a grave marker. POV Petra. Beat: mourning transmuted into peace.

chapters.title: Leeward
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Petra and Juno sail the repaired Kestrel toward new wrecks, carrying no map and no debt. Asked who she is, Petra answers simply: a diver. POV Petra. Beat: quiet resolution — inheritance refused, identity claimed.
